Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show the source mug itself moved to the right of the headphones, rather than merely adding another mug there?
node.criteria: Compare the source and edited images to identify the source mug and assess its position relative to the headphones. Pass only when visual evidence reliably supports that the source mug itself is now to the right of the headphones. Fail when evidence reliably establishes that the source mug was not moved there, such as a clearly identifiable source mug remaining at its former position while a different mug appears on the right. Use unknown when the former-position blur, scale, lighting, appearance changes, or other ambiguity prevents reliable determination of the source mug's identity or movement. A mug appearing on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved.
node.binding: Cross-image binding: the source image's blue mug, identifiable by its distinctive body and handle, and the same headphones visible in both source and edited images. Compare their corresponding regions and relative positions across images; allow for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

node_traces.evidence: The source blue mug is clearly left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug appears to the right of the headphones, but the source mug's former area is a blurred blue patch and the right-side mug looks different in color and appearance. The image does not reliably establish whether the source mug itself was moved or whether another mug was added.

d2: The binding is malformed and ambiguous (“in the (...)”), and the trace’s confident pass conflicts with the reference aggregate. The edited image shows a mug on the right of the headphones, but also a mug on the left and a conspicuous blurred blue remnant at the source mug’s original position; this is evidence of partial progress, not proof that the requested move is complete. Keep the final right-of relation check, but make the binding explicitly target the edited image and the mug/headphones, and ensure the decision distinguishes that relation from whether the source mug was moved. The current criteria already state this distinction, so inspect why the executable node/aggregation is not preserving it rather than weakening or deleting checks. Treat the unresolved aggregate/zero coverage despite a valid, queried, high-confidence pass as a routing, schema, or dependency/aggregation inconsistency—not negative visual evidence. Verify the node’s output is mapped into the rubric’s partial-progress judgment; do not force a label from the reference or infer completion from the right-side mug alone.
